candidate: The Ding Dong Tree (copper beech), Prestonpans, Scotland
verify_notes: Two sources confirm the facts: treeoftheyear.org 2017 contest page (GPS N 55 57'14.43'' W 2 58'31.14'' converts to 55.954008,-2.975317, matching the brief exactly) and East Lothian Courier local press (multiple pieces including 'Prestonpans' iconic Ding Dong Tree heading for retirement'). Species and age check out: copper beech (Fagus sylvatica f. purpurea), approx 30 years old in 2017 (so roughly 39 now), named for a schoolyard tig/tag game where children race to touch the trunk shouting Ding Dong. BLOCKED for two independent reasons, either alone sufficient. (1) ACCESS: the tree stands inside the working playground of Prestonpans Primary School, used daily by children as an outdoor classroom; no source gives any evidence of public access, no public path, no open weekends, nothing. This is exactly the school case this project's access doctrine reserves for a lead rather than a page: sending strangers onto an active schoolyard fails hard rule 10 absent real evidence of open grounds, and none exists here. (2) TOO YOUNG WITH NO COMPENSATING REASON: at roughly 30-39 years old it is far below any genuinely-old bar, it is an ordinary copper beech with no reported unusual size, shape or girth, and its remarkable quality is entirely a beloved-by-one-school-community story rather than anything a stranger could stand in front of and find worth the walk. The East Lothian Courier piece reports the tree is being retired on concerns over its long-term future, with a successor sapling (son of Ding Dong) already planted beside it, so its own remaining lifespan is itself in question. Recommend leaving this off the leads list entirely rather than filing it as a lead: it is not a temporary evidence gap, the access block is structural (an active school playground) and unlikely to change.

LOCATION CONTRADICTION RESOLVED: the coordinate given in the brief (52.068331, 6.875) is near Enschede/Overijssel and is WRONG. It appears to be a stray or mismatched value on the contest's own page, which itself is internally split: the same treeoftheyear.org 2022 page's 'Region' field and story text both say 'Maasniel, province of Limburg' and 'The Lime Tree next to the rectory in Maasniel', but its printed GPS line (N 52 4'5.99'' E 6 52'30'', which converts exactly to the brief's 52.068331,6.875) does not match that place at all. Confirmed independently: Nominatim/OSM puts Maasniel (a district of Roermond, Limburg) at 51.198,6.012, roughly 110km from the contest page's own GPS figure. Every other source agrees on Maasniel: BNNVARA Vroege Vogels ('de lindeboom van Maasniel'), Limburg24 ('boom pastorie Maasniel'), and a Monumentaal magazine piece giving the street as Pastoor Ramakerstraat, Maasniel (near Roermond). So: the real town is Maasniel/Roermond, Limburg. The Overijssel/Enschede coordinate in the lead data and on the contest page is simply an error; do not use it, and do not treat ens_006 (Enschede) as the nearest published tree for this candidate, since the tree is not near Enschede at all. VERIFIED FACTS (two independent sources beyond the contest page: BNNVARA and Monumentaal/Limburg24): summer lime (Tilia platyphyllos), planted probably in 1870 by pastor Ramakers, so roughly 150 years old as of the 2022 contest (matches contest's stated age); pruned into a distinctive three-tier 'etagelinde' shape over the years, visible as protrusions on the trunk; circumference reported as 4.5m (girth_cm 450) and height almost 25m; famous for having its own Instagram account (3000+ followers) started by the rectory's current resident. BLOCKED ON ACCESS (hard rule 10), not on evidence: the tree stands in the private garden of the pastorie (rectory), an inhabited dwelling, in Pastoor Ramakerstraat, Maasniel. BNNVARA's own piece is explicit that this is private property ('al is de boom particulier bezit') and that the garden doors 'regularly' open for visitors, which reads as occasional/by-invitation access tied to the resident's presence, events and village festivities, not standing public access with no permission needed. That is exactly the 'front gardens, courtyards of dwellings, private houses and their grounds stay out, whatever the register says and however fine the tree' case in this project's rules, and it does not bend on fame. Would need explicit evidence of scheduled, standing open hours (a price-and-a-schedule case) to reconsider; none found. Recorded as blocked rather than a lead because the block is about whose land it is, not a gap in our own research.

candidate: The Old Chestnut of Sint-Rafael, Sint-Job-in-'t-Goor, Antwerp, Belgium
verify_notes: Two independent sources beyond the contest page confirm the facts: VRT NWS (Belgian public broadcaster, 2024-10-21, 'Majestueuze kastanje van 200 jaar oud uit Sint-Job-in-'t-Goor') and general web coverage of OC Clara Fey's own announcement. Contest page GPS N 51 17'31.46'' E 4 34'59.35'' converts to 51.292072,4.583153, matching the brief exactly; confirmed against OSM/Nominatim, which places the Sint-Rafael school building at 51.2924,4.5824, metres away. Species and age check out: Sweet Chestnut (Castanea sativa), 190-200 years old per VRT, matching the contest's 150-200 year estimate; circumference more than 6 metres per VRT (girth_cm approx 600+, a genuinely large trunk for the species, though the exact figure is VRT's rounded 'meer dan 6 meter' rather than a precise register measurement, so record as girth_cm: 600+ and flag the roundness). The tree stands at the heart of Campus Sint-Rafael, part of OC Clara Fey, run by the Broeders van Liefde (Brothers of Charity). BLOCKED ON ACCESS (hard rule 10): OC Clara Fey / BuBaO Sint-Rafael (Kerklei 44, 2960 Sint-Job-in-'t-Goor, Brecht) is a care and special-education campus for children and adults with disabilities, not a public park or an ordinary school with a public-feeling yard. VRT's own piece describes it only as 'hun terreinen' (their grounds) belonging to the care organisation, with no mention of any public access, and the only public-facing event found in searches is an annual 'Dag van de Zorg' open day, which is the opposite of standing access: it exists precisely because the site is normally closed. This is a stricter case than an ordinary school (which this project already treats as needing real evidence of open grounds): it is a residential/day-care facility for a vulnerable population, and there is no source anywhere suggesting the public may walk onto the grounds to see this tree. No public path was found crossing the site. Recommend NOT filing as a lead pointing future passes back at these grounds; if OC Clara Fey ever opens a specific public viewing arrangement for the tree, that would need to come from their own institutional statement, not from us assuming access. Distance/day-trip note for the record even though moot: Sint-Job-in-'t-Goor is a separate village (Brecht municipality) roughly 15km from Antwerp centre, which would have needed its own place container rather than folding into Antwerp's page; that question does not need answering now that the tree is blocked on access.
